video.title: Beer Talk: What is a Pale Ale vs. IPA vs. Double IPA?! - Ep. #1301

read.bigIdea: American ales that lead with hops.
read.where: **American pale ale** (popularized by Sierra Nevada in **1980**) is hop-forward with **citrus, pine** and **tropical** American hops, balanced by malt: about **4.5–6.2% ABV**. **American IPA** is hoppier, more **bitter** and stronger: about **5.5–7.5%**, with a dry finish. A **session IPA** keeps the hop aroma at **5% ABV or under**.
read.mixup: IPA isn’t a measure of strength. Session IPAs are hoppy but light in alcohol.
read.sayIt: If you like hoppy, our IPA is citrusy and bitter. Want something lighter? Try a session IPA.

video.title: What even is New England IPA? | The Craft Beer Channel

keyPoints.line: less bitter than a regular IPA.

read.bigIdea: An IPA that’s juicy, not bitter.
read.where: The **hazy** (New England) IPA came from **New England** in the **2010s**. Lots of **oats and wheat** and heavy **dry hopping** make it **cloudy**, **soft** and **juicy**: tropical, stone fruit and citrus aromas, with **less bitterness** than a regular IPA. It’s usually strong: about **6–9% ABV**.
read.mixup: The haze isn’t a fault here. It’s part of the style.
read.sayIt: It’s a hazy IPA: juicy and soft, not very bitter.

video.title: Wheat Beer vs. Witbier vs. Hefeweizen. What's the difference? - Inside the Brackets Ep.25

keyPoints.line: banana and clove from the yeast.

read.where: German **Hefeweizen** (Weissbier) is at least half **wheat malt**. Its yeast makes **banana** and **clove** flavors, with a thick head and very low bitterness. Belgian **witbier** uses unmalted wheat and is spiced with **coriander** and dried **orange peel**; Hoegaarden brought the style back in 1966. Both are pale, **cloudy** and highly **carbonated**.
read.mixup: Hefeweizen’s banana and clove come from the yeast, not added fruit or spice. Witbier’s orange and coriander are added.
read.sayIt: It’s a wheat beer: light, a little citrusy, very easy drinking.

video.title: Introduction to Belgian Beer & Lambic - Master Cicerone® Rich Higgins Beer Lesson

read.where: Belgian yeast brings **fruit** and **spice**. A **dubbel** is deep reddish-copper with **raisin** and **plum** and a dry finish (about 6–7.6%). A **tripel** is **pale gold**, spicy and fruity, very dry and fizzy, and **strong**: about **7.5–9.5%**, though it hides it. **Saison** is a dry, highly carbonated farmhouse ale from French-speaking Belgium, often **peppery**.
read.mixup: A pale Belgian isn’t a light beer. A tripel can be twice as strong as a lager.
read.sayIt: Heads up, it’s about 9%. It drinks lighter than it is.

video.title: Porter and Stout: What's the difference? | The Craft Beer Channel

read.where: **Irish (dry) stout** is black, with a **coffee-like roast** from roasted barley, and dry to quite bitter. On draft it’s usually poured on **nitro** for a creamy texture, and at **3.8–5% ABV** it’s **lighter in alcohol** than most IPAs. **Porter** came first, in **London** in the early 1700s: dark brown with **chocolate** and **caramel** and gentler roast. American porter is stronger and hoppier.
read.mixup: Stout and porter overlap. Porter is usually softer and less roasty; stout drier and more coffee-like.
read.sayIt: It’s dark, but it’s actually lighter than an IPA.

video.title: Beer School: how is sour beer made? | The Craft Beer Channel

keyPoints.line: tart, a little salt and coriander.

read.where: **Berliner weisse** is very pale, low in alcohol (2.8–3.8%) and very fizzy, with a clean **lactic** sourness. **Gose** is a tart wheat beer brewed with a little **salt** and **coriander**. Most modern quick sours are **kettle soured**: the wort is soured with lactic bacteria before fermentation, for a clean, lemony tartness. **Mixed-fermentation** sours use yeast and bacteria, often in barrels, for a sour and **funky** beer.
read.mixup: A sour on purpose isn’t the same as a beer gone sour from dirty lines. One is the style; the other is a fault.
read.sayIt: It’s tart, almost like lemonade. Want a taste first?

sources: BJCP 2021 Style Guidelines, 10A, 13C, 15B, 18B, 20A, 21A, 21C, 23A, 23G, 24A, 25B, 26B, 26C, 28B, 28D (bjcp.org); Brewers Association, 2026 Beer Style Guidelines; Cicerone, US Certified Beer Server Syllabus v6.0, 2024 (cicerone.org). Checked Nov 8, 2026.
